summary: - _a) “_ Condone _the delay in completion of subject assets on merit of the same being out of the control of Petitioner in line with CERC Regulations’2019 22(2) “uncontrollable factors” and approve the tariff as claimed._ - _b) Admit the capital cost as claimed in the Petition and approve the Additional Capitalization incurred/projected to be incurred._ - _d) Allow the petitioner to recover the shortfall or refund the excess Annual Fixed Charges, on account of Return on Equity due to change in applicable Minimum Alternate/Corporate Income Tax rate as per the Income Tax Act, 1961 (as amended from time to time) of the respective financial year directly without making any application before the Commission as provided in Tariff Regulation 2019 as per para 31 above for respective block._ - _h) Allow the petitioner to claim the overall security expenses and consequential IOWC on that security expenses as mentioned at para 32 above._ - _i) Allow the petitioner to claim the capital spares at the end of tariff block as per actual._ _and pass such other relief as the Commission deems fit and appropriate under the circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice.”_ 6. The hearing in this matter was held on 20.11.2025, and the order was reserved. 7. This order is issued considering the submissions made by the Petitioner in the instant Petition vide affidavit dated 14.6.2024, affidavit dated 26.5.2025 in response to the technical validation letter 9.5.2025 and affidavits dated 17.6.2025 and 3.9.2025 in response to RoP, reply of BSPHCL vide affidavit dated 15.7.2025 & rejoinder of the Petitioner to the reply of BSPHCL vide affidavit dated 1.9.2025. 8. Having heard the learned counsel for BSPHCL and the representatives of the Petitioner and after careful examination of the material placed on record, we proceed to dispose of the Petition. 14. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions. After perusal of the documents placed on record, it has been observed that the Petitioner has not provided the CMD Certificate as required in accordance with Regulation 26(3)(a) of IEGC 2023. Therefore, the Petitioner is directed to submit the requisite CMD period; however, the Petitioner has submitted that the work could not immediately compared to the LPA of the region, were unforeseen and uncontrollable on the part of the Petitioner. The Petitioner is aware of the hindrance caused by the rains during schedule. However, it is reiterated that in the instant case, the unprecedented nature of the events had affected the works being carried out by the Petitioner in the postmonsoon period. _“There has to be a ‘real reason’ and a ‘real justification’ which the Court would consider in order to invoke a Force Majeure clause”._ The Petitioner relied upon IMD data reporting cumulative rainfall for the Nalanda district as a whole; the transmission asset was located specifically in Biharsharif, which is only one part of the district. Rainfall patterns can vary significantly within a district, and district-wide averages cannot be presumed to reflect the precise conditions at the specific project site. Even assuming but not admitting that there is any effect of such rainfall on the project site, the Petitioner is required to make efforts with due diligence and to mitigate the effect and had the Petitioner done so, the Petitioner could have achieved commercial operation in a timely. BSPHCL has submitted that under clause 14.4 of the Model TSA, timely notice of the force majeure event is a clear pre-condition to claim any relief. In the absence of any demonstrated compliance with this requirement, the entitlement to such relief is questionable. Therefore, the Petitioner’s claim for condonation of a 30-day time over-run on account of rainfall is liable to be rejected. Further, the Petitioner has not provided any reasoning for the cascading effect beyond 30 days. 46. We have considered the Petitioner’s and BSPHCL’s submissions and perused the material available on record. After perusal, it has been observed that the Petitioner has submitted the paper cuttings in support of its time claim, which are general in nature and do not substantiate the time over-run in the execution work of the transmission asset due to the imposition of Section 144 of the CrPC in Biharsharif. with due diligence and to mitigate the effect; had the Petitioner done so, the Petitioner could have achieved commercial operation promptly. **------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------** Page **25** Order in Petition No. 448/TT/2024 79. In response, the Petitioner has reiterated its submissions made in the Petition. **------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------** Page **38** Order in Petition No. 448/TT/2024 92. The Petitioner has claimed the reimbursement of the fee paid by it for filing the Petition and publication expenses. The Petitioner has further submitted that it is entitled to the reimbursement of the filing fee and the expenses incurred on publication of notices in the application for approval of tariff directly from the beneficiaries or the long- term customers, as the case may be, in accordance with Regulation 70(1) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. 93. We have considered the Petitioner's submissions. The Petitioner is entitled to reimbursement of the fee paid for filing the Petition and publication expenses incurred on this count directly from the beneficiaries or long-term customers in terms of Regulation 70(1) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. 107. This order disposes of Petition No. 448/TT/2024 in terms of the above discussions and findings.
